plan: [ This is strategically equivalent to a sealed-bid second-price auction: your sealed bid sets your exit price and, if you win, you pay the second-highest bid. In such auctions, truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy. With value 4, bid 4 to win only when competitors’ bids are below 4, capturing positive surplus V − second-highest. Overbidding risks paying above value; underbidding risks missing profitable wins. No prior rounds exist to learn from, so follow the dominant strategy. ]

[ This is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. With independent private values and risk-neutrality, bidding my true value is a (weakly) dominant strategy. Overbidding risks paying more than my value if others also bid high; underbidding risks losing when the price would have been below my value. There’s no prior history to exploit and only one round, so no learning or signaling value. Therefore, I bid my exact value of 23 to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This two-stage auction is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. The dominant strategy with independent private values is to bid truthfully. Overbidding risks paying more than my value if the second-highest bid lies between my value and my bid; underbidding risks losing profitable wins when the second-highest bid lies between my underbid and my value. There is only one round, so no signaling or learning benefits. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value, $32. ]
